question: It is characteristic of the epithelia:

options.opa: Present a binding complex in its basal region.
options.opb: Join the basement membrane by means of hemidesmosomes and focal adhesions.
options.opc: Present desmosomes just below its free surface.
options.opd: Contain intermediate filaments of vimentin and desmin (tonofilaments)

analysis: Epithelia are sheets of cells that cover body surfaces and line cavities. They are characterized by the presence of a binding complex in their basal region, which helps anchor them to the basement membrane. Desmosomes are also present in epithelia, but they are typically found in the lateral regions of the cells, not just below the free surface. Intermediate filaments in epithelial cells are typically made of cytokeratins, not vimentin and desmin.
